date_scope_check.qualification:
R6-EA-007-FU1: May 13, 2022 marks restoration of conditional cargo permission at the Myanmar–Laos Friendship Bridge. The initial COVID closure date and actual first commercial passage are unknown. Only the driver and conductor were permitted at designated transfer places under vaccination and testing conditions; ordinary passenger entry and exit remained prohibited. The retrospective report supports a prolonged interruption, but not an exact total or uniform suspension of every category.

Later actual goods access: the Trade Department reports Myanmar-to-Laos aquatic and agricultural exports through Kenglat during April–July 2023, establishing some outbound commercial access by July 31, 2023 at latest. It also reports 22 tonnes of tobacco exported in the first week of September 2023 (September 1–7). The Ministry of Information published this account on September 12; that is the report date, not the movement date. Neither interval establishes the first restored cargo crossing, unrestricted bilateral trade or passenger reopening.

CNI’s January 2024 account describes a four-year closure, which conflicts with the documented May 2022 cargo permission and actual 2023 exports. Its January 25 reopening ceremony is not treated as the first cargo reopening or proof of continuous closure since 2020.
